chapter_theme: Firmness in action is firmness of mind, and nothing else substitutes for it. Speaking is easy and doing is hard, but one who stays firm gets what he has thought of, however small he looks and whatever pain lies on the way.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter: what firmness is (661), its branches (662-663), its difficulty (664), its distinction (665), its fruit (666), how to recognise those who have it (667), how they act (668-669), and the low standing of those without it (670).

661.reading: What is called firmness in action is one's firmness of mind; all else is something other.
661.nuance: Parimelazhagar points to the word choice: மற்றைய admits these others are related, and பிற denies that they count here. Manakkudavar takes 'the others' to be means and methods.

662.reading: Avoiding harm beforehand and not giving way once it has come are, those who have studied it say, the path of these two.
662.nuance: Parimelazhagar traces the maxim to the ministers of gods and demons, Jupiter and Venus, and so explains why clean action slips in here. The verse itself mentions only 'those who have studied'.

positions.position: Avoid deeds likely to fail, and don't flag if fate spoils a deed. He rejects the variant ஓரார் as ungrammatical.
positions.quote: பழுதுபடும் வினைகளைச் செய்யாமையும், செய்யும் வினை தெய்வத்தான் பழுதுபட்ட வழி அதற்குத் தளராமையும்

positions.position: Reading ஓரார்: don't dwell on the suffering that action involves, and if it comes, don't weaken.
positions.quote: வினை செய்யுங்கால் உறும் துன்பத்தை ஓரார் ஆதலும்

positions.position: Work to remove obstacles before they come, and don't lose heart if they still do.

663.reading: True manliness is doing it so that it comes round only at the end; if it comes round midway, it brings unending trouble.
663.nuance: The verb கொட்க carries the verse, and firmness comes out as secrecy on one reading and as persistence on the other. The two make different claims about what ஆண்மை is.

positions.position: கொட்க means becoming known: conceal the deed until its end, for enemies who learn of it midway will block it.
positions.quote: செய்யப்படும் வினையை முடிவின்க புலப்படும் வகை முன்னெல்லாம் மறைத்துச் செய்வதே திட்பமாவது

positions.position: கொட்க means turning back: go through to the end and return, for returning midway brings harm.
positions.quote: ஒரு வினையைத் தொடங்கினால், முடிவிலே சென்று மீளல் செய் வது ஆண்மையாவது

664.reading: Speaking is easy for anyone; doing as one has spoken is hard.
664.nuance: Pope's 'shape one's life' turns it into a general moral. Both early commentators restrict it to the plan: saying 'this is how we will do this'. After a full chapter on eloquence, this comes as a quiet correction.

665.reading: The firmness in action of those great in excellence, once it takes effect on the king, comes to be held in everyone's regard.
665.nuance: On Parimelazhagar's reading the fruits lodge in the king, wealth and fame being his; the minister's firmness earns only regard. Kalaignar seems to have the firmness attract the ruler instead, so what ஊறெய்தி describes is unclear.

666.reading: What people have thought of, they obtain as they thought of it, if those who thought it turn out firm.
666.nuance: The first line sounds unconditional, and it is often quoted that way. The condition is in the second line: thinking must be backed by firmness. Parimelazhagar adds that such people don't think otherwise.

667.reading: Do not scorn anyone for how they look: the great rolling chariot has its linchpin.
667.nuance: The image answers the appearance: the pin bears great loads because it is placed exactly at the point of strain. Parimelazhagar applies this to small-bodied ministers while Manakkudavar applies it to everyone (யாவரையும்).

668.reading: With the deed one has looked at clearly and decided, act unwaveringly and without delay.
668.nuance: Sequence matters: கலங்காது before துளங்காது. Clarity comes first, then speed, and Parimelazhagar notes that a confused mind makes what should be dropped seem worth doing. தூக்கம் here is delay, not sleep as in Pope's 'unslumbering'.

669.reading: Even though pain closes in, do resolutely the deed that yields joy.
669.nuance: Parimelazhagar uses technical language to weigh momentary pain of effort (கணிகம்) against the lasting pleasure of the result (பரிணாம இன்பம்). The verse only says 'joy-yielding'.

670.reading: Whatever other firmness they have attained, the world doesn't want those who don't want firmness of action.
670.nuance: வேண்டாரை வேண்டாது mirrors the rejection. Parimelazhagar reads உலகு as 'the high', and Pope's gloss has 'the great', but the verse's own word is the world.

links.note: 381 makes six assets (army, people, wealth, ministers, friends, fortress) the mark of a lion among kings. Parimelazhagar's 'others' in 661 are exactly army, fort and friendship, which he says don't count as firmness. The list of assets is empty without the mind that uses them.

Two versions of the same promise: obtaining what one thinks of is easy if one keeps thinking of it (540), and if one is firm (666). The first asks for attention to be sustained, and the second for action to be.

628 prevents pain by not desiring pleasure. 669 accepts pain for the sake of the pleasure that results. One asks you to stop wanting joy and the other to work for it. They may differ in scope, since 628 speaks of how one meets pain and 669 of which tasks to take up, but neither verse says so.

source_issues: 665: Parimelazhagar's lemma for the second line is run together with its gloss, so the words ஊறெய்தி உள்ளப் படும் are not set out separately.
666: The verse reads எய்து where the metre and Parimelazhagar's lemma require எய்துப. Manakkudavar's commentary is marked as not aligned.
